blocks.text: Śiva Sūtras 2.9
blocks.directed: [long pause] Śiva Sūtras 2.9

blocks.text: ज्ञानमन्नम्
blocks.directed: [slowly] ज्ञानमन्नम्

blocks.text: Jñānam annam.
blocks.directed: Jñānam annam.

blocks.text: Knowledge is food.
blocks.directed: Knowledge is food.

blocks.text: Śiva Eats Your Thoughts for Breakfast.
blocks.directed: Śiva Eats Your Thoughts for Breakfast.

blocks.text: Now this is absolutely glorious.
blocks.directed: Now this is absolutely glorious.

blocks.text: Because Vasugupta has been playing a very sophisticated game with the word jñāna.
blocks.directed: Because Vasugupta has been playing a very sophisticated game with the word jñāna.

blocks.text: Remember 1.2?
blocks.directed: Remember 1.2?

blocks.text: ज्ञानं बन्धः।.
blocks.directed: [slowly] ज्ञानं बन्धः।.

blocks.text: Jñānaṃ bandhaḥ.
blocks.directed: Jñānaṃ bandhaḥ.

blocks.text: Knowledge is bondage.
blocks.directed: Knowledge is bondage.

blocks.text: And now?
blocks.directed: And now?

blocks.text: ज्ञानमन्नम्।
blocks.directed: [slowly] ज्ञानमन्नम्।

blocks.text: Jñānam annam.
blocks.directed: Jñānam annam.

blocks.text: Knowledge is food.
blocks.directed: Knowledge is food.

blocks.text: So we’ve gone from knowledge being the prison to knowledge being lunch.
blocks.directed: So we’ve gone from knowledge being the prison to knowledge being lunch.

blocks.text: Quite an upgrade.
blocks.directed: Quite an upgrade.

blocks.text: Let’s unpack it.
blocks.directed: Let’s unpack it.

blocks.text: Jñāna — knowledge.
blocks.directed: Jñāna — knowledge.

blocks.text: Anna — food, that which is eaten.
blocks.directed: Anna — food, that which is eaten.

blocks.text: And Kṣemarāja offers two interconnected interpretations.
blocks.directed: And Kṣemarāja offers two interconnected interpretations.

blocks.text: The first is especially powerful.
blocks.directed: The first is especially powerful.

blocks.text: The limited knowledge previously described as bondage is now food for the realised yogi.
blocks.directed: The limited knowledge previously described as bondage is now food for the realised yogi.

blocks.text: The yogi devours it.
blocks.directed: The yogi devours it.

blocks.text: Not by forgetting everything.
blocks.directed: Not by forgetting everything.

blocks.text: Not by becoming incapable of ordinary thought.
blocks.directed: Not by becoming incapable of ordinary thought.

blocks.text: And certainly not by physically eating books.
blocks.directed: And certainly not by physically eating books.

blocks.text: Although that might explain some academic departments.
blocks.directed: Although that might explain some academic departments.

blocks.text: The devouring is a metaphor for the absorption of limited knowledge into nondual recognition.
blocks.directed: The devouring is a metaphor for the absorption of limited knowledge into nondual recognition.

blocks.text: Imagine a thought arises.
blocks.directed: Imagine a thought arises.

blocks.text: “There is something separate from me.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “There is something separate from me.”

blocks.text: Under ordinary conditions, this differentiated cognition reinforces the structure of bondage.
blocks.directed: Under ordinary conditions, this differentiated cognition reinforces the structure of bondage.

blocks.text: The object appears independent.
blocks.directed: The object appears independent.

blocks.text: The subject appears limited.
blocks.directed: The subject appears limited.

blocks.text: The relationship between them is experienced through separation.
blocks.directed: The relationship between them is experienced through separation.

blocks.text: But now suppose the fundamental reality of consciousness has been recognised.
blocks.directed: But now suppose the fundamental reality of consciousness has been recognised.

blocks.text: The same differentiated appearance occurs.
blocks.directed: The same differentiated appearance occurs.

blocks.text: A sound.
blocks.directed: A sound.

blocks.text: A colour.
blocks.directed: A colour.

blocks.text: A sensation.
blocks.directed: A sensation.

blocks.text: A thought.
blocks.directed: A thought.

blocks.text: But its ultimate nature is no longer misunderstood.
blocks.directed: But its ultimate nature is no longer misunderstood.

blocks.text: The difference appears within the undivided field of consciousness.
blocks.directed: The difference appears within the undivided field of consciousness.

blocks.text: And therefore the difference no longer necessarily obscures its conscious source.
blocks.directed: And therefore the difference no longer necessarily obscures its conscious source.

blocks.text: This is what Kṣemarāja means by the devouring of limited knowledge.
blocks.directed: This is what Kṣemarāja means by the devouring of limited knowledge.

blocks.text: The distinction is not necessarily annihilated at the level of conventional functioning.
blocks.directed: The distinction is not necessarily annihilated at the level of conventional functioning.

blocks.text: Instead, its apparent independence is overcome.
blocks.directed: Instead, its apparent independence is overcome.

blocks.text: A wave appears.
blocks.directed: A wave appears.

blocks.text: The ocean does not cease to be the ocean.
blocks.directed: The ocean does not cease to be the ocean.

blocks.text: And the wave, recognised in its true nature, is never something fundamentally foreign to the water.
blocks.directed: And the wave, recognised in its true nature, is never something fundamentally foreign to the water.

blocks.text: Now imagine the yogi encountering the entire universe in this manner.
blocks.directed: Now imagine the yogi encountering the entire universe in this manner.

blocks.text: Each differentiated cognition becomes an occasion for recognising its source.
blocks.directed: Each differentiated cognition becomes an occasion for recognising its source.

blocks.text: The world is no longer a collection of alien objects confronting a finite subject.
blocks.directed: The world is no longer a collection of alien objects confronting a finite subject.

blocks.text: It is the manifestation of consciousness, continually recognised.
blocks.directed: It is the manifestation of consciousness, continually recognised.

blocks.text: And there’s something extraordinarily affirmative about this.
blocks.directed: And there’s something extraordinarily affirmative about this.

blocks.text: Because the yogi doesn’t have to become incapable of perceiving differences.
blocks.directed: Because the yogi doesn’t have to become incapable of perceiving differences.

blocks.text: They don’t have to destroy the mental faculty that makes ordinary life possible.
blocks.directed: They don’t have to destroy the mental faculty that makes ordinary life possible.

blocks.text: They don’t have to wander around insisting that chairs and elephants are literally identical at every empirical level.
blocks.directed: They don’t have to wander around insisting that chairs and elephants are literally identical at every empirical level.

blocks.text: That would be a terrible way to organise a zoo.
blocks.directed: That would be a terrible way to organise a zoo.

blocks.text: Instead, differences are apprehended without mistaking them for ultimate separations in consciousness.
blocks.directed: Instead, differences are apprehended without mistaking them for ultimate separations in consciousness.

blocks.text: The second interpretation Kṣemarāja offers is equally beautiful.
blocks.directed: The second interpretation Kṣemarāja offers is equally beautiful.

blocks.text: Knowledge of the Self becomes food through the satisfaction it produces.
blocks.directed: Knowledge of the Self becomes food through the satisfaction it produces.

blocks.text: The yogi is nourished by recognition.
blocks.directed: The yogi is nourished by recognition.

blocks.text: And the term tṛpti — satisfaction or fulfilment — becomes relevant.
blocks.directed: And the term tṛpti — satisfaction or fulfilment — becomes relevant.

blocks.text: Not a temporary pleasure requiring another object.
blocks.directed: Not a temporary pleasure requiring another object.

blocks.text: But the fullness associated with resting in one’s own conscious nature.
blocks.directed: But the fullness associated with resting in one’s own conscious nature.

blocks.text: This recalls the Trika understanding of ānanda as intrinsic to the supreme reality.
blocks.directed: This recalls the Trika understanding of ānanda as intrinsic to the supreme reality.

blocks.text: You’re not acquiring completeness from an external object.
blocks.directed: You’re not acquiring completeness from an external object.

blocks.text: You’re recognising the completeness fundamental to consciousness.
blocks.directed: You’re recognising the completeness fundamental to consciousness.

blocks.text: Kṣemarāja draws on the Vijñānabhairava and Spandakārikā to make these points. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.
blocks.directed: Kṣemarāja draws on the Vijñānabhairava and Spandakārikā to make these points. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.

blocks.text: And now notice the beautiful progression of the preceding two sūtras.
blocks.directed: And now notice the beautiful progression of the preceding two sūtras.

blocks.text: At 2.8, the body is offered into consciousness.
blocks.directed: At 2.8, the body is offered into consciousness.

blocks.text: At 2.9, limited knowledge is consumed by consciousness.
blocks.directed: At 2.9, limited knowledge is consumed by consciousness.

blocks.text: First, the embodied identity is relinquished as the ultimate Self.
blocks.directed: First, the embodied identity is relinquished as the ultimate Self.

blocks.text: Then differentiated cognition is absorbed into recognition.
blocks.directed: Then differentiated cognition is absorbed into recognition.

blocks.text: The fire consumes the body.
blocks.directed: The fire consumes the body.

blocks.text: Consciousness consumes knowledge.
blocks.directed: Consciousness consumes knowledge.

blocks.text: And throughout this sacrificial imagery, there is no second reality outside Śiva.
blocks.directed: And throughout this sacrificial imagery, there is no second reality outside Śiva.

blocks.text: The offerer, the offering, and the act of consumption are manifestations of his own power.
blocks.directed: The offerer, the offering, and the act of consumption are manifestations of his own power.

blocks.text: This is what makes Trika so magnificent.
blocks.directed: This is what makes Trika so magnificent.

blocks.text: The same consciousness that manifested the universe now recognises it through the very powers by which it was manifested.
blocks.directed: The same consciousness that manifested the universe now recognises it through the very powers by which it was manifested.

blocks.text: The world hasn’t become spiritually irrelevant.
blocks.directed: The world hasn’t become spiritually irrelevant.

blocks.text: It has become the meal.
blocks.directed: It has become the meal.

blocks.text: And apparently Śiva has quite the appetite.
blocks.directed: And apparently Śiva has quite the appetite.
